question: ____ was the founder of the Widow Remarriage Association (1861)
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahadev Govind Ranade**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mahadev Govind Ranade was a distinguished Indian scholar, social reformer, and author.
 
• He co-founded the Widow Remarriage Association in 1861, which advocated for the rights and remarriage of widows.
 
• Ranade was one of the founding members of the Indian National Congress and played a significant role in India's social and political movements.
 
• He was also a judge of the Bombay High Court and a staunch supporter of social reforms such as the abolition of child marriage and the promotion of women's education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Keshub Chandra Sen**

 
 
• Keshub Chandra Sen was an influential Indian social reformer who was associated with the Brahmo Samaj.
 
• He worked towards the abolition of sati, child marriage, and the promotion of women's education.
 
• He established the Indian Reform Association in 1870, which aimed at promoting social and educational reforms.
 
 
 
• **Dr. Atma Ram Pandurang**
 
 
• Dr. Atma Ram Pandurang was a notable Indian physician and social reformer.
 
• He was one of the founders of the Prarthana Samaj, which aimed at reforming social customs and religious practices in India.
 
• He worked towards the upliftment of women and the eradication of caste discrimination.
 
 
 
• **Debendra Nath Tagore**
 
 
• Debendra Nath Tagore was an eminent Indian philosopher and religious reformer, associated with the Brahmo Samaj.
 
• He was the father of Rabindranath Tagore, the famous poet and Nobel laureate.
 
• He played a crucial role in the Brahmo Samaj movement, which aimed at reforming Hindu society and religion.
